mainTopic: Is ויהי בנסוע a separate ספר? Saving the margins of a ספר תורה from a fire, and how to treat ספרי מינין and the debate houses of the מינין.
overview: This עמוד opens by finishing a ברייתא about the special marks around the פרשה of ויהי בנסוע הארון. The תנא קמא says the marks show the פרשה is out of place. רבי says they show it is a ספר of its own, which is why רבי יונתן can speak of 'seven books of the Torah.' רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the פרשה was put here to separate two punishments, and רב אשי says it really belongs in the section of the דגלים. The גמרא then asks whether the blank margins (גליונות) of a ספר תורה may be saved from a fire on שבת. It tries four proofs: a worn-out scroll, an erased scroll, the rule that margins make hands טמא, and a ברייתא about burning margins. It pushes off every one, so the question is never decided. That last ברייתא leads into the laws of ספרי מינין. רבי יוסי says to cut out and bury the שמות, while רבי טרפון and רבי ישמעאל say even the שמות may be burned, because heretics knowingly deny ה׳. The עמוד ends with stories about the debate house בי אבידן and begins a story about אימא שלום that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The first opinion: the section is not in its place
steps.stepSummary: The end of the תנא קמא's reason for the marks around ויהי בנסוע הארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...because this is not its place.
steps.whatsHappening: We pick up in the middle of a ברייתא. The first opinion is giving its reason for the special marks around the פרשה of ויהי בנסוע הארון: the פרשה is not in its proper place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous page, the ברייתא said this פרשה has marks (סימניות) before and after it. According to the תנא קמא, the marks signal that this paragraph was moved here from somewhere else. The verses right before it do not talk about the camp traveling, so it does not fit here.

keyTerms.meaning: special marks placed around the פרשה (from the previous page)
'And it was when the Ark traveled' (במדבר י:לה-לו)

phrases.english: because this is not its place.
phrases.notes: This finishes the תנא קמא's words that started back on 115b.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The marks show that the פרשה of ויהי בנסוע is displaced from its proper location.

steps.title: רבי: the section is a book of its own
steps.stepSummary: רבי gives a different reason for the marks: this פרשה counts as an independent ספר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: It is not for that reason. Rather, it is because it is considered a book by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי disagrees with the reason just given. He says the marks are there because this short פרשה counts as a separate book.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marks mean something different according to רבי. They do not show that the פרשה was moved. They set it apart as an independent ספר. As a result, ספר במדבר is split into three parts.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, editor of the משנה
it is not for that reason

steps.whyThisMatters: This view is the basis for the הלכה that 85 letters (the length of this פרשה) count as a 'ספר' for saving from a fire, as we will see below.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
it is not for that reason,
rather, because it is considered a book
by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִן הַשֵּׁם הוּא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the reason given in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פרשה of ויהי בנסוע is an independent ספר.

steps.title: Whose view fits the 'seven pillars' teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion matches the teaching that 'seven pillars' refers to seven books of the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom is what רבי שמואל בר נחמן said in the name of רבי יונתן: 'She carved out her seven pillars' — these are the seven books of the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a teaching that the Torah has seven books. It asks which side of the dispute this teaching follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we count five חומשים. Saying there are 'seven books' needs an explanation. The question invites us to match this teaching to one of the two opinions above.

keyTerms.meaning: according to whom does it go?
'she carved out her seven pillars' (משלי ט:א)

phrases.english: According to whom is this
that Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said
Rabbi Yonatan said:
'She carved out her seven pillars,'
these are the seven books of the Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects an outside teaching to the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view is the source for 'seven books of the Torah'?

steps.title: It follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: The teaching of seven books follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? According to רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'seven books' teaching follows רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ויהי בנסוע is its own ספר, then במדבר becomes three books: the part before it, the פרשה itself, and the part after it. Add בראשית, שמות, ויקרא, and דברים, and you get seven.
steps.confusionAlert: There are not literally seven scrolls. 'Seven books' is a way of counting the sections, based on רבי's view that במדבר divides into three.

phrases.english: — According to whom? According to Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It follows רבי, since he divides במדבר into three books.

steps.title: Who disagrees with רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the opposing view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who disagrees with רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to put a name on the anonymous first opinion, the one that says the פרשה is out of place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא presented the opposing view without a name. The גמרא looks for a known תנא who holds it, so that we can see that view more fully.

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who disagrees with Rabbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from רבי's side to the opposing side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds the 'not in its place' view.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the section will one day be moved
steps.stepSummary: It is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says this פרשה will in the future be uprooted and written in its proper place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, as it was taught: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: In the future this פרשה will be uprooted from here and written in its proper place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and quotes a ברייתא to show he holds that the פרשה is out of place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רשב"ג does not treat this פרשה as its own book. To him it is a misplaced paragraph that will be moved back to where it belongs in the future.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: — It is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
In the future this portion will be uprooted from here
and written in its proper place.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הוּא. דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 and brings a ברייתא as the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says the פרשה is displaced and will be returned to its place.

steps.title: Why the section was placed here: to separate two punishments
steps.stepSummary: רשב"ג explains that the פרשה was placed here to create a break between two punishments.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was it written here? To make a break between the first punishment and the second punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, רשב"ג asks and answers his own question: if the פרשה is out of place, why is it here? It is here to separate two stories of punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two stories of the people sinning would otherwise stand right next to each other. The Torah put this פרשה between them as a pause, so that the bad events would not run one after another.

phrases.english: And why did it write it here?
— In order to separate
between the first punishment and the second punishment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the current placement of a פרשה that is out of place.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is placed here to separate two accounts of punishment.

steps.title: The second punishment: the complainers
steps.stepSummary: The second punishment is the story of the people who complained.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the second punishment? 'And the people were like complainers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The text identifies the second punishment as the story that comes right after the פרשה: the people complained, and a fire broke out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the verse right after ויהי בנסוע (במדבר יא:א). It is clearly a story of sin and punishment.

phrases.english: What is the second punishment?
— 'And the people were like complainers.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines a term from step 7.

steps.title: The first punishment: running away from סיני
steps.stepSummary: The first 'punishment' is that they traveled from הר ה׳. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא explains this means they turned away from following ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first punishment: 'And they traveled from the mountain of ה׳.' And רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: This means they turned away from after ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The text identifies the first event. On the surface the verse is only about traveling, so an אמורא explains why it counts as a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving הר סיני sounds innocent. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא reads it as running away eagerly from ה׳, like children escaping school. That makes it a real failing, and so the verse can be called the first פורענות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'they traveled from the mountain of ה׳' (במדבר י:לג)
that they turned away from after ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: The 'first punishment' is really the sin of leaving הר סיני in a hurry, not a punishment described in the verse. רבי חמא's reading is what turns a travel verse into a story of failing.

phrases.english: The first punishment:
— 'And they traveled from the mountain of ה׳,'
and Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
that they turned away from after ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the other term from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Leaving סיני eagerly, which is read as turning away from ה׳.

steps.title: Where does the section really belong?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the proper place of this פרשה is, according to רשב"ג.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is its proper place?
steps.whatsHappening: Since רשב"ג said the פרשה will be moved to its real place, the גמרא asks where that place is. This sets up רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'its place' but never said where that is. The גמרא fills in the missing detail.

phrases.english: And where is its place?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a detail missing from step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The proper location of ויהי בנסוע.

steps.title: רב אשי: in the section about the banners
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the פרשה belongs in the section about the דגלים (the tribal banners).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: In the section of the banners.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that the פרשה belongs in the section of the דגלים, which describes how the tribes traveled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויהי בנסוע is about the Ark traveling. The section of the דגלים (במדבר ב, in the parasha of במדבר סיני) describes the order of the camp when it traveled. A paragraph about traveling fits naturally there.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא, editor of the תלמוד בבלי
banners: the section describing the tribes' camp and travel order

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: ויהי בנסוע is its own ספר, which is why the Torah has 'seven books.' רשב"ג: it is out of place. It was put here to separate two punishments and belongs in the section of the דגלים.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
In the section of the banners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Its place is in the section of the דגלים.

steps.title: Do we save the blank margins of a Torah scroll from a fire?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: may the blank parts (גליונות) of a ספר תורה be rescued from a fire on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: The blank margins of a ספר תורה — do we save them from a fire, or do we not save them from a fire?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Do the blank, unwritten parts of a ספר תורה have enough קדושה to be saved from a fire on שבת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows saving holy writings from a fire on שבת. The question is whether parchment with no letters on it shares that status, since it is part of a holy scroll.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked among them

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
The blank margins of a Torah scroll —
do we rescue them from the fire

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין מַצִּילִין אוֹתָן מִפְּנֵי הַדְּלֵיקָה?
phrases.english: or do we not rescue them from the fire?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, related to the laws of saving holy writings on שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether blank parchment of a ספר תורה may be rescued from a fire on שבת.

steps.title: Attempted proof from a worn-out Torah scroll
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a worn-out ספר תורה is saved only if it still has 85 letters, the length of ויהי בנסוע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A ספר תורה that wore out — if it still has enough to gather 85 letters, like the פרשה of 'ויהי בנסוע הארון,' we save it. If not, we do not save it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. It is setting up a proof that will be spelled out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number 85 comes from ויהי בנסוע. Following רבי's view, that small פרשה counts as a full ספר, so 85 letters are the minimum for a 'book.' The ברייתא says a scroll with fewer letters is not saved.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links the two halves of this passage: רבי's view that ויהי בנסוע is a ספר sets the minimum size of 'holy writing' for this הלכה.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A Torah scroll that wore out —
if there is in it enough to gather
eighty-five letters,
like the portion of 'And it was when the Ark traveled'
— we rescue it,
and if not, we do not rescue it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That blank margins are not saved.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a worn-out ספר תורה with fewer than 85 letters.

steps.title: The proof spelled out: why not save it for its margins?
steps.stepSummary: If margins were saved, the worn scroll would be saved for its blank parts. Since it is not saved, margins must not be saved.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not? Let it be saved because of its own blank margins!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the proof. Even a worn-out scroll has blank margins. If margins could be saved, we should save it because of them. Since the ברייתא says not to save it, margins must not be saved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is asked like a challenge, but its job here is to finish the proof. It shows that the ברייתא only makes sense if blank margins have no rescue status.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַמַּאי, תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם גִּילָּיוֹן דִּידֵיהּ!
phrases.english: But why? Derive it [that it is rescued] because of its own blank margins!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי, תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִשּׁוּם גִּילָּיוֹן דִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא in step 13.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא does not allow saving a worn scroll, even though it has margins.

steps.title: Rejection: a worn-out scroll is different
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. A worn-out scroll has lost its קדושה, so its margins are not holy. Margins of an intact scroll may still be saved.
steps.simpleTranslation: A worn-out scroll is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא was about a worn-out scroll, which is a special case. So it tells us nothing about the margins of a normal ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Margins are holy only because they belong to a holy scroll. Once the scroll is worn out, it no longer counts as a ספר תורה, so its margins lose that status too. The original question about a whole scroll's margins is left open by this source.
steps.whatToRemember: The question about saving גליונות is not answered by the worn-scroll ברייתא. That ברייתא deals with a scroll whose קדושה is already gone, so its margins are not proof either way.

phrases.english: A worn-out [scroll] is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of steps 13-14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only; the question in step 12 stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source deals with a worn scroll that has lost its קדושה, so its margins are not holy. It cannot show what applies to the margins of an intact scroll.

steps.title: An erased scroll should be saved because of its margins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא about an erased ספר תורה. It asks why such a scroll is not saved because of its blank margins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a ספר תורה that was erased is saved if 85 letters can still be gathered from it, like the פרשה of ויהי בנסוע הארון. If not, it is not saved. But why? It should be saved because of its own margins!
steps.whatsHappening: After the worn-out scroll proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a second proof from a different ברייתא, about a scroll whose writing was erased. It points out the problem: if margins are holy, even an erased scroll should be saved for its margins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous proof failed because a worn-out scroll has lost its קדושה entirely. An erased scroll is a different case: the parchment is intact, and its blank parts should be no worse than ordinary margins. So if margins had their own קדושה, the scroll should be saved for them, yet the ברייתא says a scroll with fewer than 85 letters is not saved.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא introduces a source as a proof
Derive it from [another reason]; it should already follow from
A blank margin or blank area of a scroll

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A Torah scroll that was erased,
if there is enough in it to gather
eighty-five letters,
like the portion of 'And when the Ark traveled'
— we rescue it,
and if not — we do not rescue it.
But why?
Derive that it is saved because of its own blank margins!
phrases.notes: If margins are holy, the scroll should be saved for their sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attempt to answer step 12, after the worn-scroll proof was rejected in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That margins of a ספר תורה are not saved on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about an erased ספר תורה needing 85 letters

steps.title: The question is only about true margins, not erased writing space
steps.stepSummary: The space where writing used to be loses its holiness once the writing is gone. The question is only about the real margins: top, bottom, between sections, between columns, and at the beginning and end of the scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: The place of the writing is not my question. It was holy only because of the writing, and once the writing is gone, its holiness is gone. My question is about the margins above and below, between one section and another, between one column and another, at the beginning of the scroll, and at the end of the scroll.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by narrowing what it is really asking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An erased scroll mostly has blank space where letters once stood. That space was holy only because of the letters, so it is not like a true margin. The real question is about margins that were always blank, so the ברייתא proves nothing about them.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the writing was
Here: a column or sheet of the scroll

steps.confusionAlert: Two kinds of blank space are in play. One is erased writing space, which loses its holiness. The other is true margins, which is the open question.

phrases.english: The place of the writing is not my question,
because when it was holy —
it was holy because of the writing;
once the writing is gone —
its holiness is gone.
What I am asking about is
the margins above and below,
those between one section and another,
those between one column and another,
those at the beginning of the scroll and at the end of the scroll.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 16 by separating erased writing space from true margins.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full: the ברייתא says nothing about true margins
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof treated erased writing space as if it were a margin

steps.title: But the erased scroll still has real margins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that even an erased scroll still has its true margins. So it should be saved because of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then derive that it is saved because of those margins!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. An erased scroll still has its top, bottom, and side margins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Erasing the letters does not remove the true margins. If those margins were holy, the scroll should still be saved, so the proof seems to return.

keyTerms.meaning: That one; here, those true margins

phrases.english: Then derive that it is saved because of that [true margin]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is irrelevant to true margins
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An erased scroll still has true margins, so if margins were saved, the scroll would be saved too

steps.title: The margins were cut off and thrown away
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is speaking of a scroll whose margins were cut off and discarded.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the margins were cut off and thrown away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining the case the ברייתא has in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא's case, only the erased writing area is left. No true margins remain, so nothing could make the scroll worth saving. The question about margins stays open.

phrases.english: Where the margins were cut off and thrown away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The erased scroll still had its true margins
steps.terutzMaskana: The margins were removed, so only the erased writing space was left

steps.title: Margins make hands טמא, so they must be holy
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says the margins of a scroll make hands טמא. That suggests margins have the holiness of a ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the margins above and below, between sections, between columns, at the beginning of the scroll, and at the end of the scroll make the hands טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third proof. Margins are treated like the holy writing itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים decreed that holy scrolls make hands טמא, and this משנה applies the rule to margins too. If margins count as holy for this law, maybe they are also holy enough to be saved from a fire.

keyTerms.meaning: Make the hands ritually impure, a rabbinic rule for holy scrolls

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The blank margins above and below,
those between one section and another,
those between one column and another,
those at the beginning of the scroll and at the end of the scroll —
make the hands ritually impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַגִּלְיוֹנִין שֶׁל מַעְלָה וְשֶׁל מַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new attempt to answer the question from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That margins are holy and may be saved
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that margins make hands טמא

steps.title: Margins attached to the scroll are different
steps.stepSummary: Margins may be holy only while attached to the ספר תורה. The question is about margins on their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps when they are part of a ספר תורה, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the third proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks of margins that are still part of a whole scroll. There they share the scroll's holiness. That tells us nothing about margins that stand alone, so the question is still open.

phrases.english: Perhaps when they are part of a Torah scroll, it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 20.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה deals with attached margins, not separate ones

steps.title: A ברייתא says margins are left to burn
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says margins and ספרי מינין are not saved and burn where they are. The גמרא suggests this means margins of a ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: margins and ספרי מינין are not saved from a fire. They burn where they are, they and the names of ה׳ in them. Doesn't this mean the margins of a ספר תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth proof. It seems to say directly that margins are not saved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'גליונין' here means margins of a kosher ספר תורה, this would answer the question with a no. The words 'מאי לאו' show the גמרא is offering this reading.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The blank margins and the books of heretics
are not rescued from the fire;
rather, they burn in their place,
they and the names of God in them.
Is this not about the margins of a Torah scroll?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth attempt to answer the question from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That margins of a ספר תורה are not saved
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about גליונין and ספרי מינין

steps.title: The margins are those of heretical books
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means the margins of ספרי מינין, not of a kosher ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means the margins of the books of heretics.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the fourth proof by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the margins belong to heretical books, the ברייתא says nothing about a real ספר תורה, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: No; the proposed reading is rejected

phrases.english: No, the margins of the books of heretics.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading proposed in step 22.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may not be talking about a kosher ספר תורה

steps.title: Why mention the margins of heretical books at all?
steps.stepSummary: If even the ספרי מינין themselves are not saved, there is no need to say their margins are not saved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if the books of heretics themselves are not saved, do we even need to say it about their margins?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading: it makes the ברייתא say something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The written parts of a heretical book are more significant than its blank edges. If the books are not saved, their margins clearly are not either. So listing the margins would be pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Now; if even this is true
Is it even necessary to say?

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא סִפְרֵי מִינִין גּוּפַיְיהוּ אֵין מַצִּילִין,
phrases.english: Now, if the books of heretics themselves are not rescued,
is it necessary to say so about their margins?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא סִפְרֵי מִינִין גּוּפַיְיהוּ אֵין מַצִּילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading גליונין as margins of ספרי מינין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, mentioning the margins would add nothing

steps.title: Heretical books are treated like blank margins
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means that ספרי מינין have the same status as blank parchment.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: the books of heretics are like blank margins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא to answer the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not listing two separate items. It is comparing heretical books to blank parchment, which has no קדושה of its own. Even the שמות in them do not make them holy. The ברייתא still proves nothing about margins of a kosher ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
And the books of heretics are like blank margins.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: וְסִפְרֵי מִינִין הֲרֵי הֵן כְּגִלְיוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists margins and heretical books as two items
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא compares heretical books to blank parchment
steps.whatToRemember: All four proofs about margins were pushed off: the worn-out scroll, the erased scroll, the טומאת ידים rule, and the ברייתא about burning. The question about saving the margins of a ספר תורה is still not resolved.

steps.title: The ברייתא about heretical books quoted again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to study the ברייתא about ספרי מינין for its own sake.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: margins and ספרי מינין are not saved from a fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion. It quotes the ברייתא again so it can bring the rest of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'גופה' means the גמרא is now studying the ברייתא directly, not as a proof. The repeated line prepares for the opinions of רבי יוסי and רבי טרפון.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; studying a source directly

phrases.english: The matter itself:
The blank margins and the books of heretics
are not rescued from the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the margins question to studying the ברייתא itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heretical books and margins are not saved from a fire on שבת

steps.title: רבי יוסי: cut out the שמות and bury them
steps.stepSummary: On a weekday, one cuts out the names of ה׳ from heretical books, buries them, and burns the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: on a weekday, one cuts out the names of ה׳ in them and buries them, and burns the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי explains what to do with heretical books on a regular weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי still respects the written שמות of ה׳, so he says to bury them (גניזה). The rest of the book has no holiness and is burned.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
On a weekday one cuts out the names of God in them
and buries them,
and the rest — he burns.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: בַּחוֹל קוֹדֵר אֶת הָאַזְכָּרוֹת שֶׁבָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי יוסי's view on weekday treatment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cut out and bury the שמות, then burn the rest

steps.title: רבי טרפון swears to burn them, שמות and all
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון swears that he would burn heretical books, including the names of ה׳ in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said: I swear by my sons that if these books come into my hands, I will burn them along with the names of ה׳ in them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון disagrees with רבי יוסי and takes a much harsher position, stated as an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי יוסי, רבי טרפון would not even save the שמות. In his view, books written by heretics carry no holiness at all.

keyTerms.meaning: May I bury my sons (a strong oath)

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said:
May I bury my sons,
that if they come into my hands
I will burn them
and the names of God in them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן: אֲקַפֵּחַ אֶת בָּנַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A stricter view that disagrees with רבי יוסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burn heretical books together with their שמות

steps.title: Heretics are worse than idol worshippers
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון explains that heretics are worse than idol worshippers because they know the truth and deny it anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if someone is chasing a person to kill him, or a snake is rushing to bite him, he should run into a house of עבודה זרה rather than into the houses of these heretics. Idol worshippers do not know ה׳ and deny Him, but heretics know ה׳ and still deny Him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון gives the reason for his harsh view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An idol worshipper denies ה׳ without knowing Him. A heretic knows the truth and rejects it on purpose, which is far worse. That is why their books deserve no respect, even the שמות in them.

keyTerms.meaning: They recognize the truth and deny it
To bite him (said of a snake)

steps.confusionAlert: 'הללו' appears twice and refers to different groups. The first 'הללו' is the heretics, who know and deny. The second is the idol worshippers, who do not know and deny.

phrases.english: For even if a person is chasing him to kill him,
and a snake is running to bite him,
he may enter a house of idol worship
but may not enter the houses of these heretics,
because these heretics know God and deny Him,
while those idol worshippers do not know Him and deny Him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי טרפון's oath.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heretics who knowingly deny ה׳ are worse than idol worshippers

steps.title: A verse about putting ה׳ behind the door
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון quotes a פסוק in ישעיה that describes heretics as people who push ה׳'s memory behind the door.
steps.simpleTranslation: About them the verse says: 'Behind the door and the doorpost you have placed your memory.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון brings a פסוק to support his description of the heretics.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heretics remember ה׳ but push Him aside on purpose, as if hiding Him behind a door. This matches 'they know and deny,' and it supports burning their books.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on heretical books. רבי יוסי says to cut out and bury the שמות and burn the rest. רבי טרפון says to burn everything, because heretics know ה׳ and still deny Him, which makes them worse than idol worshippers.

phrases.english: And about them the verse says:
'Behind the door and the doorpost
you have placed your memory.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי טרפון's reasoning from step 29 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That heretics knowingly push ה׳ aside

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's קל וחומר from the סוטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל proves with a קל וחומר from סוטה that ה׳'s names in heretical books may be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: there is a קל וחומר. To make peace between a husband and wife, the תורה says: let My name, written in holiness, be erased in the water. These heretics bring jealousy, hatred and strife between ישראל and their Father in Heaven. All the more so may ה׳'s name be erased because of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives a logical proof for רבי טרפון's harsh position that even ה׳'s names in heretical books can be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a סוטה, the תורה lets ה׳'s name be erased just to bring peace inside one home. Heretics damage the much bigger relationship between ישראל and ה׳. So if erasing the name is allowed for the smaller goal, it is certainly allowed for the bigger one.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument. If a rule applies in a lighter case, it surely applies in a stronger case.
Will be erased in the water. This refers to the סוטה ritual, where ה׳'s name is dissolved in water.
How much more so. This is the closing formula of a קל וחומר.

steps.whyThisMatters: Normally erasing ה׳'s name is forbidden. This קל וחומר explains why the rule is different for ספרי מינין.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said: it is an a fortiori argument:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה לַעֲשׂוֹת שָׁלוֹם בֵּין אִישׁ לְאִשְׁתּוֹ
phrases.english: Just as, to make peace between a man and his wife,
the Torah said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמִי שֶׁנִּכְתַּב בִּקְדוּשָּׁה יִמָּחֶה עַל הַמַּיִם,
phrases.english: My name, which was written in holiness, shall be erased in the water,
phrases.notes: This is the סוטה ritual (במדבר ה).

phrases.english: these, who cast jealousy, hatred and rivalry
between Israel and their Father in Heaven —
how much more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a logical proof to רבי טרפון's position on burning the names.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳'s names in ספרי מינין may be destroyed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the erasing of ה׳'s name in the סוטה ritual

steps.title: David's verse about hating God's enemies
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in תהלים shows that דוד המלך hated those who rebel against ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: About them דוד said: 'Do I not hate those who hate You, ה׳, and quarrel with those who rise up against You? I hate them with complete hatred; they have become my enemies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to show that heretics deserve to be treated as enemies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר showed that destroying their books is permitted. This פסוק adds the attitude behind it. Those who fight ה׳ are enemies, not just people who made a mistake, so their writings get no protection.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who rise up against You

phrases.english: And about them David said:
"Do I not hate those who hate You, O Lord,
and quarrel with those who rise against You?
I hate them with utmost hatred;
they have become enemies to me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the קל וחומר with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That heretics are to be treated as enemies

steps.title: Heretical books are not saved from any destruction
steps.stepSummary: Just as we do not save ספרי מינין from a fire, we do not save them from any other kind of destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as we do not save them from a fire, we also do not save them from a collapse, from water, or from anything else that destroys them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא widens the rule. It is not only about fire on שבת. We do not save these books from any danger at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה talks about saving holy writings from a fire on שבת. This line makes clear that ספרי מינין are not holy writings in any sense, so the reason they are left to burn has nothing to do with שבת. We would not save them from a collapsing building or a flood either.

keyTerms.meaning: A collapse, such as a falling building or rockslide

steps.whatToRemember: ספרי מינין have no holiness. We may destroy them, even the names of ה׳ written in them, and we never rescue them.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין מַצִּילִין אוֹתָן מִפְּנֵי הַדְּלֵיקָה,
phrases.english: And just as we do not rescue them from the fire,
so too we do not rescue them

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִן הַמַּפּוֹלֶת וְלֹא מִן הַמַּיִם
phrases.english: not from a collapse and not from water
and not from anything that destroys them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין מַצִּילִין אוֹתָן מִפְּנֵי הַדְּלֵיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by widening the rule beyond fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספרי מינין are not rescued from fire, collapse, water, or any other destruction.

steps.title: Do we save the books of בי אבידן?
steps.stepSummary: יוסף בר חנין asks רבי אבהו whether the books of בי אבידן are saved from a fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: יוסף בר חנין asked רבי אבהו: the books of בי אבידן, do we save them from a fire or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is raised about a case in between. These are books found in a place where Jews and non-Jews debated religion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These books were not clearly heretical books, and they were also not plainly ordinary holy books. Some say they were Jewish holy texts that were kept in a debate house. The question is whether the place they were kept in, or the way they were used, takes away their holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him. Used to introduce a real question.
A house where religious debates took place

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ יוֹסֵף בַּר חָנִין מֵרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ:
phrases.english: Yosef bar Chanin asked of Rabbi Abahu:
These books of the house of Avidan,
do we rescue them from the fire
or do we not rescue them?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ יוֹסֵף בַּר חָנִין מֵרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from clear heretical books to a doubtful case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the books of בי אבידן have the status of holy books that are rescued

steps.title: רבי אבהו is unsure
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers 'yes and no.' The question stays unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said 'yes' and 'no,' and the matter was shaky in his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו does not give a clear answer. The question is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase means רבי אבהו himself was in doubt. There were reasons on both sides, so no ruling is given.

keyTerms.meaning: It was loose, meaning uncertain, in his hand

phrases.english: Yes and no, and it was uncertain in his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question, but without settling it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No clear answer. רבי אבהו was in doubt.

steps.title: רב and שמואל's practice regarding these houses
steps.stepSummary: רב avoided both בי אבידן and בי נצרפי. שמואל avoided only בי נצרפי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב did not go to בי אבידן, and certainly not to בי נצרפי. שמואל did not go to בי נצרפי, but he did go to בי אבידן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how the great אמוראים acted toward these places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בי נצרפי was a place of idol worship, so both of them stayed away from it. בי אבידן was a debate house, and there they disagreed. רב was stricter and avoided it. שמואל was willing to go there.

keyTerms.meaning: A house of idol worship, often explained as a Persian fire-temple

phrases.english: Rav would not go to the house of Avidan,
and all the more so not to the house of Nitzrefei.
Shmuel would not go to the house of Nitzrefei,
but to the house of Avidan he would go.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of בי אבידן with the behavior of רב and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב avoided בי אבידן. שמואל went there. Both avoided בי נצרפי.

steps.title: רבא's polite excuse for not coming
steps.stepSummary: רבא avoids going to בי אבידן by using the excuse of a palm tree on the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבא: why don't you come to בי אבידן? He said: there is a certain palm tree on the road, and it is hard for me. They said: we will uproot it. He said: its place, the hole it leaves, will be hard for me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. רבא gives a polite excuse each time so that he never has to go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא did not want to insult them by refusing openly. So he named an obstacle on the road. When they offered to remove it, he said the hole left behind would also be a problem. This shows he simply did not want to go.

phrases.english: They said to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָתֵית לְבֵי אֲבִידָן?
phrases.english: Why don't you come to the house of Avidan?
He said to them:
There is a certain palm tree on the road,
and it is difficult for me.
They said: We will uproot it.
He said: Its place will be difficult for me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְרָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָתֵית לְבֵי אֲבִידָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another אמורא's attitude toward בי אבידן, told as a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא avoided בי אבידן, using polite excuses.

steps.title: מר בר יוסף's confidence and the danger
steps.stepSummary: מר בר יוסף said he was not afraid of them, but once when he went they tried to endanger him.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר יוסף said: I am one of them, and I am not afraid of them. One time he went, and they tried to endanger him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of an אמורא who felt safe going to them, and then found out it was dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בר יוסף thought his good relationship with them protected him. The story shows that going there was a real danger. This supports the חכמים who stayed away.

phrases.english: Mar bar Yosef said:
I am one of them,
and I am not afraid of them.
One time he went,
and they sought to endanger him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אֲנָא מִינַּיְיהוּ אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the stories about going to these debate houses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even someone friendly with them was put in danger, which shows the risk.

steps.title: Nicknames for the heretics' gospel book
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר called their book 'און גליון' and רבי יוחנן called it 'עון גליון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר called it 'און גליון', a page of wickedness. רבי יוחנן called it 'עון גליון', a page of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records how two sages, the תנא רבי מאיר and the אמורא רבי יוחנן, mocked the name of the Christian gospel book with insulting wordplays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Greek name for the book sounded a bit like these Hebrew phrases. By twisting the name into words meaning 'wickedness' and 'sin,' they showed that this book has no holiness at all. This fits the earlier ruling that such books are not saved.

keyTerms.meaning: A wicked page. A wordplay on the gospel's name.
A sinful page. Another wordplay on the same name.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הֲוָה קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״אָוֶון גִּלְיוֹן״.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir would call it "aven gilyon" (wicked page).

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״עֲווֹן גִּלְיוֹן״.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan would call it "avon gilyon" (sinful page).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds how the חכמים viewed the heretics' main book.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The heretics' gospel book is treated as wicked and sinful, with no holiness.

steps.title: Introducing the story of אימא שלום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story about אימא שלום, the wife of רבי אליעזר and sister of רבן גמליאל, and a philosopher who lived near them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אימא שלום, the wife of רבי אליעזר, was the sister of רבן גמליאל. There was a certain philosopher in their neighborhood...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא introduces the people in a new story, which continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story will show the dishonesty of a Christian judge-philosopher. That links back to the topic of the מינין. Here we only meet the main characters.

phrases.english: Imma Shalom, the wife of Rabbi Eliezer,
was the sister of Rabban Gamliel.
There was a certain philosopher in his neighborhood

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story connected to the topic of the מינין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the characters of a story that continues on the next amud.
